AFDREV

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Reno NV
135 PM PST Sat Nov 21 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

* Well-below seasonal normal temperatures continue today underneath 
  cloudy skies.

* A weak storm will bring periods of light valley rain and snow 
  tonight through Sunday, with minor travel impacts in the Sierra.

* Holiday travel will be most ideal Monday into Tuesday, disrupted 
  by another storm Tuesday night or Wednesday. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...

For today, model guidance shows an upper ridge over the region 
with a PacNW trough close behind it. By tonight, the ridge is 
projected to move off to the east as a weak shortwave moves 
through N California. With this setup aloft, mostly dry weather is
in store for the region through this afternoon. Well-below normal
temperatures (highs in the mid-30s to mid-40s) will continue 
today with increasing cloud coverage through the day limits 
daytime heating potential. Going into tonight, portions of NE 
California and far NW Nevada begin to see around a 30-70% chance 
for light snow showers, though little to no accumulation is 
expected through the night. Sierra ridge winds also increase this 
evening through tomorrow morning with gusts up to around 50-70 mph
out of the southwest. There may also be some choppy lake 
conditions tonight with Lake Tahoe winds gusting up to around 25 
mph. While cold overnight temperatures are in the forecast, the 
increased cloud cover will allow for low temperatures to be around
10 degrees warmer than the lows experienced over the previous
night.

On Sunday, models project another trough moving through the region 
causing the wintry shower chances to spread into the Sierra and W 
Nevada by the late morning and afternoon hours. These shower chances 
will continue through the evening before tapering off overnight. The 
18Z run of the HRRR model is also showing a band of showers 
setting up along I-80 between 10 AM-6 PM PT, which could cause 
hazardous travel conditions for those traveling along that route. 
When looking at the latest forecast snowfall totals, amounts 
appeared to have trended a bit downward compared to the overnight 
package. New snowfall amounts at the Sierra crest generally look 
to be between 1-3 inches by Monday morning with a 20-40% NBM 
probability of greater than 3 inches of snow. There is a 40-60% 
NBM probability of 0.1+ inches of snow at Lake Tahoe and a 50-70% 
chance of the same in foothill communities such as Virginia City 
as well, so these areas could see a few tenths of an inch of snow 
possible. Snow levels will rise above the valley floor (~4500-5000
ft) on Sunday afternoon allowing showers to produce rain or a 
rain- snow mix, but then will drop again in the evening 
transitioning precipitation type to snow. Not expecting much 
accumulating snowfall if any for the Reno-Sparks area at this 
time, but cannot rule it out completely. Keep in mind that roads 
and surfaces may be slick through the night especially when 
temperatures drop below freezing.

On Monday through early Tuesday: forecast guidance shows an upper 
ridge moving into the region signaling drier conditions coming out 
of the weekend. If you have Thanksgiving travel plans, this looks to 
be the best time to travel ahead of the holiday. Recent wintry 
precipitation may keep roads and surfaces slick for a bit and there 
may be potential for freezing fog in some locations during the cold 
mornings on Monday and Tuesday, so please use caution if 
traveling. The dry pattern does not look to last too long as 
another trough moves through late Tuesday into Wednesday though 
models currently disagree with timing. This system does look to be
wetter though a bit warmer, so impactful snowfall could be 
confined to higher elevations. Will be monitoring this going 
forward especially if winter products need to be issued, but there
is still some good forecast uncertainty with this system. 

Beyond the midweek system, ensemble guidance is showing another 
ridge moving over the western CONUS, which signals warmer and 
drier weather by Thanksgiving Day. However, the latest run of the 
NBM does have precipitation chances returning to the region late 
Friday into following weekend. -078

&&

.AVIATION...

KRNO Forecast: VFR conditions continue through the rest of today and 
into tonight, with relatively light winds and a scattered to broken 
cloud deck. SW FL100 winds increase to 30 kts around 22/04Z, 
allowing for LLWS and mountain wave turbulence concerns through 
around 22/12Z.

Regional Outlook: VFR conditions continue today with relatively 
light winds and increased cloud cover through the region. 
Increasing SW FL100 winds will introduce LLWS and mountain wave 
turbulence issues after 22/00Z. 10-30% of -SHSN at KTRK-KTVL 
expected after 22/06Z. Showers near KTRK could cause sub-VFR CIGs 
around 22/13Z, but low confidence to add to TAF at this time. 

24-72 Hour Outlook: Increasing chances for light snow across E 
Sierra terminals between 22/18Z-23/03Z, occasionally reducing 
CIGS/VIS to MVFR or briefly IFR conditions. Chances of rain or a 
rain-snow mix increase to 20-40% late Sunday morning for KRNO- 
KCXP-KMEV, becoming -SN Sunday night. A period of dry weather 
Monday into Tuesday will allow better flight conditions, before 
the next storm arrives Tuesday night.

-Salas/078
